system_type_reason: Deployable digital-human voice agent (Go server + Python inference) with pluggable backends; product-oriented README.

repo_overview.summary: Real-time digital-human voice agent framework. A Go server orchestrates WebRTC sessions (direct P2P with embedded TURN, or LiveKit SFU) and calls a Python gRPC inference server hosting pluggable ASR/LLM/TTS/omni-voice/RAG/avatar backends. A PersonaAgent wraps a realtime omni model (Qwen Omni / Doubao) and delegates long-running work (search, research, reports) via native tool calls to background LangGraph SubAgents with their own LLM tool loop.

components.purpose: Go core: session lifecycle, turn pipeline ASR->LLM->TTS->avatar, interruption handling, idle avatar runtime
Go gRPC clients to the Python inference server
WebRTC transport: Pion P2P with embedded TURN, LiveKit bot, media segments
REST API (characters, settings, knowledge, offline videos) and WebSocket hub
task store, persona and chat-history persistence, RAG store, session recording, YAML/.env config
Python gRPC server, plugin registry, per-modality service adapters
agent core: PersonaAgent, Qwen Omni and Doubao realtime clients, persona/ (supervisor, local task runtime, LangGraph SubAgent, tools)
provider plugins: OpenAI/LiteLLM/Qwen LLM, Whisper/Qwen ASR, Doubao/Qwen/OpenAI TTS, FlashHead/LiveAct avatar
embedding and retrieval engine for character knowledge
example config (session limits, timeouts, warmup), Docker files, gRPC schemas
vendored third-party avatar model code (FlashHead, MuseTalk, SoulX-LiveAct), out of coding scope
Vue web UI, out of coding scope

topology.justification: The PersonaAgent is driven by a realtime omni model (Qwen Omni or Doubao) with its own persona system prompt (persona_agent.py:69-82). Via the create_task tool it delegates to a background SubAgent that runs on a separate text LLM (llm.py, default qwen3.6-plus) with its own system prompt and its own LangGraph tool loop (agent.py:76-88, 213-218). A boss AI delegating to a helper AI with its own LLM loop counts as multi-agent, even though the delegation is exposed as a tool.

resilience.name: SubAgent iteration cap with terminal-tool completion check
resilience.what_it_is: The LangGraph SubAgent loop (llm_call <-> tool_node) routes to END once llm_calls reaches max_agent_iterations (code default 8, example config 100). If the terminal tool create_html_report was never called by then, run_subagent raises TimeoutError, which the task runtime records as a failed task.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the routing edge after each tool round of the background SubAgent. Bounds the number of LLM calls per delegated task and turns a non-converging run into an explicit failure. Otherwise a SubAgent that keeps searching and never writes its report loops indefinitely and accumulates unbounded token cost.

resilience.name: tool errors returned to the model as structured results (persona and SubAgent level)
resilience.what_it_is: SubAgent level: ZhihuToolExecutor.execute catches every exception from the Zhihu API client (HTTP errors, missing access secret) and returns {"ok": False, "error": ...}; unknown tool names and non-zero Zhihu API codes are also normalized into error objects; tool_node wraps every result into a ToolMessage for the next LLM call. Persona level: any exception while executing a persona tool (supervisor routing, task limit, RAG) becomes {"ok": False, "error": ...} and is sent to the omni model as tool_result.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between tool execution and the next model call in both loops: the SubAgent tool_node and the PersonaAgent tool-call handling inside converse_stream. Converts tool failures into observations the model can react to, e.g. rephrasing a search or telling the user that too many tasks are running, and the loop keeps running. Otherwise a single failing tool call raises out of the graph and fails the background task, or breaks the realtime voice stream.

resilience.name: background task failure isolation with spoken fallback
resilience.what_it_is: Each SubAgent runs as its own asyncio task; _run_task catches any exception and stores a task.failed event. The supervisor polls the task until a terminal status with a monitor timeout (default 1800 s, poll 1 s). On timeout or error, run_pending_task returns task_start_failed_prompt, which instructs the persona to tell the user in one natural sentence to try again later.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the background SubAgent and the realtime voice conversation. Contains SubAgent crashes and hangs inside the task and turns them into a spoken answer for the user. Otherwise a failing or hanging background task either breaks the voice session or leaves the user waiting for a result that never arrives.

resilience.name: automatic RAG grounding before each reply with failure fallback
resilience.what_it_is: After every user transcript the PersonaAgent searches the character knowledge base and sends the hits as response_instructions for the next reply, telling the model to prioritize these materials and to avoid inventing facts absent from them. If retrieval raises, the exception is logged and the reply proceeds with empty instructions.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the PersonaAgent loop between the user transcript and the omni model's response. Grounds persona answers in imported character material to reduce hallucinated biographical facts, and a retrieval failure degrades to an ungrounded reply. Otherwise the model answers character questions from its own weights, and a RAG outage blocks the reply.

resilience.name: Qwen deferred-response serialization with conflict re-queue
resilience.what_it_is: A _QwenResponseCoordinator queues every response.create request (tool result, RAG instructions, injected task result) and sends the next one only once the model is idle. When the provider answers with "Conversation already has an active response", the current request is pushed back to the front of the queue and resent later. On stream close it waits up to 60 s for outstanding responses.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the PersonaAgent's injected inputs and the Qwen Omni realtime WebSocket. Prevents replies from being dropped when a tool result or a finished background task arrives while the persona is still speaking. Otherwise the provider rejects the overlapping response.create and the user never hears the task result.

resilience.name: ASR session rollover before the provider session limit
resilience.what_it_is: The Qwen ASR sender runs against a deadline of max_session_seconds (default 540 s). On expiry it sends session.finish and returns the rollover marker, the outer loop drains late transcript events for rollover_drain_seconds (default 5 s), closes the WebSocket and opens a fresh provider session with the next queued chunk as its first audio. A producer task buffers incoming audio in a bounded asyncio.Queue (default 64 chunks) so the caller's stream keeps flowing during the swap.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the ASR plugin between the orchestrator's audio stream and the DashScope realtime WebSocket, one layer below the turn pipeline. Rotates the provider session before the provider's own session limit ends it, while the gRPC audio stream from the Go side stays open. Otherwise a conversation longer than the provider session limit loses transcription mid-turn and the voice pipeline stalls.

resilience.name: retrieval budget for RAG grounding
resilience.what_it_is: RAG search requests top_k hits (default 5), drops every hit whose converted score falls below min_score (default 0.25), and fills up to max_context_chars (default 4500), clipping the last chunk and breaking once the budget is spent. Indexing splits documents into 900-character chunks with 120 characters overlap, so a single hit stays small.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in front of the character knowledge block that the PersonaAgent injects as response_instructions before every reply. Caps how much retrieved text enters each realtime turn and filters weakly matching chunks out of the prompt. Otherwise whole documents travel into every grounded reply, which inflates per-turn token cost and the latency of a voice turn that the user waits on.

resilience.name: voice pre-flight check before a character is saved
resilience.what_it_is: The character API probes a chosen voice id against the realtime provider under a 5 s Go deadline before the voice is persisted. The Python CheckVoice handler wraps the provider probe in asyncio.wait_for with a 4.5 s timeout and reports a provider rejection as provider_error separately from a transport failure. A rejection answers 502 with the provider message, a timeout answers 503.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits on the character configuration path, ahead of every voice session that will later use that character. Moves an invalid voice id into the edit request that introduced it, where a human is present to correct it. Otherwise the bad voice surfaces when the realtime session opens and breaks the first turn of a live conversation.

resilience.name: cancellation-scoped teardown of inference streams
resilience.what_it_is: Every Go streaming helper for ASR, TTS, avatar and the omni conversation follows one shape: a sender goroutine and a receiver loop that both select on ctx.Done(), output and error channels closed via defer, and the sender joined through a buffered sendDone channel before the helper returns. The avatar helper closes its video channel before the error channel so consumers drain buffered frames first.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits under every turn of the Go pipeline, between the orchestrator and the Python inference server. Cancelling the turn context stops all provider streams of that turn together and releases their goroutines and gRPC streams. This is the effect side of an interrupted or aborted turn. Otherwise a cancelled turn leaves sender goroutines blocked on channel sends and provider streams open, and the audio of the abandoned turn keeps arriving while the next turn runs.

resilience.name: barge-in and turn interruption across orchestrator and realtime plugins
resilience.what_it_is: Three call sites in the Go orchestrator combine inference.Interrupt(sessionID) with cancelPipeline: stopPipelineAndWait used by the startup greeting and by assistant speech, handleVoiceLLMTextInput, and the explicit Interrupt entry point. A fourth trigger is the barge_in flag on an omni output, which aborts the running turn inside the pipeline loop. The gRPC Interrupt handler fans the call out to every registered omni and voice_llm plugin: Qwen Omni sends response.cancel plus input_audio_buffer.clear on the realtime WebSocket, Doubao sends a FinishSession frame.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between user input and the reply that is currently being generated and played. Ends that reply at the provider, in the Go pipeline and in the browser playback at the same time when the user speaks, sends text, or a new turn preempts the old one. Otherwise the persona keeps speaking over the user while tokens and audio are still billed for an answer nobody listens to. The teardown of the affected inference streams is covered by "cancellation-scoped teardown of inference streams".

resilience.name: monotonic turn and pipeline sequences guarding stale output
resilience.what_it_is: Every session carries two monotonic counters. MarkTurnStarted increments TurnSeq per conversational turn, MarkPipelineRunning increments PipelineSeq per pipeline goroutine. State transitions, status broadcasts and completion handling check IsCurrentTurn and IsCurrentPipeline first, and MarkPipelineFinished returns early when a stale pipeline reports completion. advancePlaybackEpoch pushes the turn sequence to the media peer, and every published AV segment carries Epoch set to that turn sequence. Aborted turns are parked in an ignoredTurns map keyed by reply or question id so that late provider output is matched back to them. On the transport side both media backends hold the epoch in an atomic that only moves forward through compare-and-swap, and they check isPlaybackStale at five stages: when a segment is enqueued, at the encoder input, after encoding, in the publisher, and inside the per-frame loop of publishAVSegment while the segment is already going out.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around the whole turn pipeline, between the provider output loop and the browser. After an interrupt or a preempting turn, output belonging to the superseded turn is discarded before publication. Otherwise audio and video segments of a dead turn reach playback and its late "speaking" and "idle" transitions overwrite the state of the turn that replaced it.

resilience.name: history capture for superseded turns
resilience.what_it_is: abortTurn marks an interrupted turn as aborted, cancels its avatar context and registers it under its reply or question key in ignoredTurns. Output that still arrives for that key goes to recordIgnoredTurnOutput, which keeps accumulating transcript and audio and, once the output is final, writes the assistant message, the raw audio, the transcript and the conversation file, and broadcasts one final assistant transcript.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits behind the barge-in path in the omni pipeline loop. The realtime provider finishes generating the aborted reply on its side, so this keeps the text in local history and in the persisted conversation. The dialog context of the next turn then matches what the model believes it said. Otherwise provider-side conversation state and local history diverge with every interruption.

resilience.name: per-turn conversation persistence with idempotent save flags
resilience.what_it_is: Assistant message, raw audio, transcript and conversation file are written by four helpers, each guarded by its own flag on the turn (historySaved, rawAudioSaved, transcriptSaved, conversationSaved) so repeated calls write once. They run when the model output turns final and again when the avatar worker for that turn completes. persistSessionConversation snapshots the session history under a read lock and writes the whole conversation through the character store.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the end of every turn in both the omni and the standard pipeline. Commits the conversation incrementally while the session is still running. A crash, a dropped WebRTC connection or an idle eviction then costs at most the turn in flight. Otherwise the session history exists only in memory until teardown and is lost whenever teardown fails to run.

resilience.name: concurrent session cap with idle eviction
resilience.what_it_is: SessionManager.Create refuses a new session with ErrMaxSessions once the live session count reaches max_concurrent (yaml value, code default 4), which the REST API turns into HTTP 503. A cleanup goroutine ticks every 30 s and evicts sessions whose LastActiveAt is older than the idle timeout, calling OnSessionEnd before removing them. LastActiveAt is refreshed by every state change, turn start and stored message.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the entry point of every new session and above all running sessions. Bounds how many GPU-backed avatar and realtime provider sessions exist in parallel, and reclaims sessions whose browser tab went away without a teardown request. Otherwise abandoned sessions hold provider connections, avatar model state and GPU capacity for the lifetime of the server. The idle timeout in effect is the 5 minutes hardcoded in NewSessionManager, the constructor the server binary uses. The config keys idle_timeout_s and max_duration_s are declared and parsed, and reading them back into the session manager is left open.

resilience.name: bounded graceful teardown
resilience.what_it_is: TeardownSession cancels the pipeline context, waits up to 3 s on the pipeline goroutine through WaitPipelineDone, stops the silent avatar runtime and waits up to 3 s for it, and only then disconnects the media peer and closes the WebSocket. WaitPipelineDone is a select over the done channel and a timer, so a hung goroutine cannot block. At the regular end of a turn the pipeline waits up to 10 s in WaitAVDrain so buffered AV segments still reach the browser. WaitAVDrain is implemented as a fence marker: a segment carrying only a Fence channel travels through encoder and publisher without being encoded, and the publisher closes that channel once every preceding segment has been published including its real-time pacing. Both the enqueue of the fence and the wait on it carry the timeout.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at session end and at the end of each turn. Gives in-flight work a bounded grace period to persist its messages and to play out buffered media. Otherwise teardown either drops the last turn including its history and recording, or blocks indefinitely on a provider stream that never returns.

resilience.name: global serialization of the shared avatar model state
resilience.what_it_is: The inference server holds one avatar image per avatar model, so a single orchestrator mutex avatarMu is held across whole generation cycles: SetAvatar plus GenerateAvatar plus frame collection in EnsureIdleVideo, the full avatar streaming loop of the standard pipeline, the per-turn avatar worker of the omni pipeline, and the entire lifetime of the silent avatar runtime. On top of that SetupSession refuses a second session while a silent-inference avatar runtime is already running.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between all concurrent users of the avatar model: parallel sessions, idle-video generation and the idle runtime. Keeps one session's avatar image installed for the whole time that session streams frames. resilience.name: idle lead filling with bounded lookahead for the persistent avatar stream
resilience.what_it_is: In silent_inference mode one avatar gRPC stream stays open for the whole session. A feed loop pushes 100 ms chunks of synthetic breathing audio into it whenever the lead, measured as model input samples minus rendered video samples, stays below maxLead. maxLead is derived from the avatar model's own chunk duration and frames-per-chunk reported by AvatarInfo, defaults to 1.2 s and is capped at 5 s. Speech items take priority over idle chunks, and idle filling stops once the active speech has produced its first video segment.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits under every turn of a silent-inference session, between the turn pipeline and the avatar model. Keeps the long-lived stream fed between turns so the avatar keeps breathing and the model stays warm across turn boundaries, with one stream setup per session. The lead cap bounds how much idle video is generated ahead of time, which is video a new reply has to queue behind. Otherwise either the stream starves between turns or the response latency of the next turn grows with the prebuffered idle backlog.

resilience.name: supersedable idle segments dropped when newer speech is queued
resilience.what_it_is: Idle filler video from the silent avatar runtime is enqueued with Supersedable set. At enqueue such a segment records the current latestSpeechEpoch as SpeechEpochAtQueue, while every segment carrying a real turn epoch pushes latestSpeechEpoch forward through compare-and-swap. The staleness check then drops any supersedable segment whose recorded speech epoch has been overtaken, at every pipeline stage down to the per-frame publish loop.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the idle avatar runtime and playback, one layer below the turn pipeline. Discards breathing video that was queued or already encoded as soon as a reply is on its way, so the reply starts playing at once. Otherwise the answer waits behind up to maxLead seconds of prerendered idle video, which adds that delay to every response. This is the playback-side counterpart of "idle lead filling with bounded lookahead for the persistent avatar stream".

resilience.name: media path reset inside a live session
resilience.what_it_is: On a direct_media_reset_request from the browser the orchestrator resends the ICE configuration and calls ResetMediaPath, which closes the old PeerConnection and rebuilds the whole media path: tracks, opus encoder, bitrate target, audio delay state, RTP gap clock and the connected channel are reset, then Connect and StartNegotiation run again. The user audio channel owned by the session survives this, and isActivePeerConnection makes every callback of the old connection a no-op.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits under the running session, between browser and orchestrator. Repairs a broken WebRTC media path while the session, its history and the realtime provider connection keep running. Otherwise a failed ICE connection ends the session, and the user restarts the conversation from an empty context.

resilience.name: bandwidth-adaptive VP8 bitrate with clamps and fallback
resilience.what_it_is: The shared webrtc.API registers GCC send-side bandwidth estimation (initial 1 Mbps, min 100 kbps, max 10 Mbps) next to NACK and TWCC. DirectPeer subscribes to the estimator with a 10 s timeout and keeps the default bitrate when none arrives. currentVideoBitrateKbps takes 65 percent of the current estimate and clamps the result into 500 to 1800 kbps, and each segment is VP8-encoded at that value. Dedicated RTCP reader goroutines run per sender so the interceptors receive browser feedback at all.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the outgoing media boundary, in front of the per-segment VP8 encode. Follows the measured uplink capacity so avatar frames keep arriving under congestion, with a hard floor, a ceiling and a fallback when the estimator stays silent. Otherwise the server encodes above the available capacity on a narrow link and segments queue up until the reply arrives late.

resilience.name: publish readiness guards against silent media loss
resilience.what_it_is: Before publishing a segment or an audio frame the direct peer waits up to 10 s in waitConnected, which also returns on pipeline cancellation, and it skips the publish when the video or audio track is missing. In the LiveKit bot ensureVideoTrackLocked polls track.IsBound() for up to 10 s and logs the timeout, because LocalTrack.WriteSample stays a silent no-op until WebRTC Bind has installed the packetizer.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the AV pipeline and the transport, at the start of every publish. Holds segments back until the connection and the tracks can actually carry them. Otherwise the first reply of a session is written into an unbound track and vanishes, while its audio plays through the separate audio track and the user sees a still image talking.

resilience.name: avatar warmup with silent inference before the first session
resilience.what_it_is: A warmup block in the config gates a silent inference pass during avatar plugin init. resolve_avatar_warmup_policy combines warmup.enabled (false when the key is absent) with warmup.distributed.enabled (true by default) and the world size, so multi-GPU runs can skip it. FlashHead pushes one silent audio slice of slice_len_samples through the pipeline and resets its local state afterwards. LiveAct runs three iterations that cover the first-chunk path, the overlap-decode path and the steady-state update_cache path. Before either runs, _distributed_all_ranks_ready reduces the per-rank init flag with all_reduce MIN, so warmup starts once every rank finished avatar setup. The parsed distributed.timeout_s value is carried in the policy and no code reads it.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at process start, ahead of the turn loop. It pays the one-time cost of kernel compilation, memory allocation and cache setup while no user is waiting. Otherwise the first turn of the first session absorbs that cost, which is exactly the moment the user waits for the avatar to speak for the first time.

resilience.name: terminal-status write guard on background tasks
resilience.what_it_is: AppendEvent and CreateArtifact load the task row inside the same transaction as the write and return ErrTerminal when the status is completed, failed or cancelled. IsTerminal defines those three states. The HTTP layer maps ErrTerminal to 409 Conflict.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the write boundary of the task store, where a background SubAgent reports progress and results. It rejects late reports from a run that already ended, cancelled runs included. Otherwise a delayed report moves a cancelled task back to running and the persona speaks a result the user called off.

resilience.name: self-disabling turn recording on any setup failure
resilience.what_it_is: BeginTurn returns nil on every failure path: recording disabled, output directory not creatable, ffmpeg stdin pipe error, ffmpeg start error. Every TurnRecording method checks its nil receiver first, so the nil value stays usable. The orchestrator treats nil as a regular state and only logs the errors returned by SaveRawAudio and SaveTranscript.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits on the live media path of each turn, where frames and PCM are forwarded to ffmpeg while they are sent to the browser. It keeps a recording failure local to recording. Otherwise a missing ffmpeg binary or an unwritable directory aborts the conversation turn itself, although recording is a side task.

resilience.name: indexing status lifecycle with persisted failure reason
resilience.what_it_is: Each knowledge source carries a status (indexing, ready, failed), an error string and a chunk count in sources.json. indexKnowledgeSource marks the source failed with the concrete error at every abort point (path not resolvable, RAG disabled, inference not configured, indexing call failed) and ready with the chunk count on success. Uploading an indexable file schedules the indexing run, and the reindex endpoint resets the status and repeats it.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between file upload and the retrieval path that grounds every reply. It records why a document never entered the index and makes the run repeatable. Otherwise the reply pipeline answers without the document the user just uploaded and the failure stays invisible.

resilience.name: path containment for model-supplied storage ids
resilience.what_it_is: validateStorageID rejects task and artifact ids that are . or .. or contain a path separator. It runs on every id supplied through the API, while ids the store generates itself are uuids. In the knowledge store, cleanRelativePath drops empty and . segments, rejects .. and sanitizes each remaining segment, while pathFromStoredPath resolves the joined path and verifies by absolute-path prefix that it stays under the character knowledge directory.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the storage boundary of the task API, where artifact ids arrive from the background SubAgent and therefore from model output. It bounds where an agent run can write. Otherwise a generated identifier places a file outside the artifact directory of its task.

resilience.name: transactional task event log with per-task sequence numbers
resilience.what_it_is: Each event takes its sequence from SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 inside the transaction that also inserts the event and updates the task row, with PRIMARY KEY(task_id, seq) enforcing uniqueness. ListEventsAfter reads the log from a given sequence onward with a clamped limit; that replay path has no caller outside the tests.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits under every status update of a background task, between the reporting SubAgent and the WebSocket broadcast to the session. It keeps the task row and its event chain in one atomic write, so status, progress and result summary stay consistent with the events the client already received. Otherwise a crash between the two writes leaves a task whose row and history disagree.

resilience.name: durable task store with WAL and serialized writes
resilience.what_it_is: OpenStore opens the SQLite file, caps the pool at one connection with SetMaxOpenConns(1) and runs the migration before the store is handed out. The migration sets journal_mode=WAL, creates every table with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and adds the later owner_id column through ensureTaskOwnerColumn, which inspects PRAGMA table_info and issues ALTER TABLE only when the column is missing.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits under the state of all background tasks, which run for minutes while the voice session continues. It carries that state across a server restart and serializes concurrent event writers from several running tasks. Otherwise parallel writes hit SQLITE_BUSY and a restart loses every task in flight.

resilience.name: artifact file rollback on failed persistence
resilience.what_it_is: CreateArtifact writes the artifact content to disk first and then inserts the database row inside the open transaction. When the insert or the commit fails, the file it just wrote is removed before the error is returned.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the end of a background task, where the SubAgent hands over the document it produced. It keeps the file tree and the artifact table consistent. Otherwise a failed insert leaves a file on disk that no task references and that no listing or cleanup path reaches.
